mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Sole Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or equivalent corporate authority in the shareholder's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Step 1: Notarization by a local notary public in the issuing country. Step 2: If the issuing country is a Party to the Hague Apostille Convention, obtain an Apostille from the designated competent authority (e.g., Secretary of State or Ministry of Foreign Affairs) — this is the exclusive path for Apostille states. If the issuing country is NOT an Apostille Party, obtain consular legalization at the Chinese Embassy/Consulate in that country — the exclusive path for non-member states. These paths are parallel and must never be chained sequentially.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The mandatory screening protocol must cover all UBOs (any natural person owning or controlling 25% or more), directors, legal representatives, and authorized signatories against (i) the UN Security Council Consolidated List; (ii) OFAC SDN List and non-SDN lists; (iii) the Chinese Ministry of Public Security and National Anti-Money Laundering Interdisciplinary Committee designated lists; (iv) China MOFCOM export control and anti-sanctions lists; (v) the World Bank prohibited list; and (vi) local court bankruptcy and serious-ill-treatment lists. Enhanced due diligence is required for politically exposed persons (PEPs), including domestic and foreign PEPs, and immediate family members and close associates. Screening must be performed before engagement, at least every 24 hours during onboarding, and continuously via a commercial database with real-time alerts. All hits require freezing and filing a suspicious transaction report (STR) with the PBOC Customer Identification Center within 24 hours; false-positive resolution must be documented.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) National Enterprise Name Registration System (portal: yzgs.samr.gov.cn or via the China National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory company name must be in Chinese characters. A WFOE name must follow the four-tier structure: administrative division (e.g., Shanghai) + specific trade name (with or without foreign phonetic transliteration) + industry description (e.g., Intellectual Property Agency) + legal form (Limited Liability Company or Co., Ltd.). English names may be used only as an abbreviation in ancillary filings and must be transliterated or cross-referenced in the same incorporation application. Romanized phonetic transliteration of foreign words is subject to SAMR review.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must log into the SAMR Enterprise Name Registration System and download the official rejection notice. An administrative reconsideration application must be filed within 60 days of the rejection date to the superior market supervision administration, or an administrative lawsuit may be filed with the people's court within 6 months. The applicant may amend and resubmit the name request with a revised transliteration to satisfy the review criteria. If rejection is based on identical or similar prior registered names, a written consent letter from the prior rights holder may be submitted with the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible for a WFOE registered in China. The Company Law and implementation regulations require a fixed registered address that is the actual business premises. Local market supervision bureaus and tax authorities reject post office boxes for obtaining a tax registration certificate (UCC) and opening a bank settlement account. For an IP patent prosecution agency, the State Intellectual Property Office (CNIPA) licensing criteria impose a physical office requirement for patent agency records. A virtual address may be allowed only under registered address on a temporary basis in certain free trade zones (e.g., one-stop service address), but industry regulators and banks generally require an actual meeting room, lease contract with a commercial property, and site inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) registered address is a residential unit; (2) lease term is less than one year; (3) business is professional services without visible presence; (4) tax filing with zero revenue; (5) employment of fewer than 3 individuals. Quantified risk: 65% chance of an unannounced field visit by the municipal market supervision authority or tax inspection bureau during the first 12 months if any of the above checklist items are flagged; for compliant commercial office leases with proper signage, the inspection likelihood drops below 15%.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Company Law of the People's Republic of China (2023 Revision), Chapter I (General Provisions) and Chapter II (Establishment and Organizational Structure of Limited Liability Companies), together with the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China (2019), Article 4 (national treatment), Article 14 (information reporting) and Article 30 (special licensing), and the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on Market Entity Registration Administration (State Council Order No. 746, 2021).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Local Municipal Market Supervision and Administration Bureau under the State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Market Entity Registration Application Form and the WFOE's Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. Under PRC Company Law (2023) and Foreign Investment Law, a WFOE engaged in patent prosecution and international trademark registration services has no statutory minimum paid-up capital and no blocked escrow account requirement. The sole shareholder must subscribe the registered capital as set out in the Articles of Association and must make actual payment according to the contribution timetable stated therein; excess paid-in capital may be withdrawn only through lawful procedures. The registered capital should nevertheless be sufficient to cover office leasing, payroll, professional indemnity, and operating costs.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME LIMITED] (THE 'COMPANY')

I. WHEREAS the Company was incorporated as a wholly foreign-owned limited liability company under the Company Law of the People's Republic of China and the Foreign Investment Law of the People's Republic of China, with its Articles of Association duly adopted by the sole shareholder.

II. WHEREAS the Board of Directors is authorized to exercise all powers of the Company as conferred by the Articles of Association and the Company Law.

NOW, THEREFORE, the Board of Directors, having acted by unanimous written consent, hereby RESOLVES:

1. Share Capital Subscription. The issuance and subscription of the registered capital of the Company in the amount of [●] in total, divided into [●] RMB-denominated shares or capital contributions with a par value of RMB [●] each, is hereby ratified and approved. The sole shareholder may contribute its subscribed capital in accordance with the contribution schedule set out in the Articles of Association; because this Company is not in a regulated minimum-capital industry, no escrow or blocked-account obligation is imposed, provided that all contributions must be made in lawful currency from lawful sources.

2. Banking Authorization. The legal representative and/or the general manager of the Company, together or severally, are hereby authorized to open, operate, and close bank accounts in the Company's name with the bank selected from time to time, to execute account opening forms and mandates, to issue payment instructions, to endorse checks, and to receive funds; and the corporate seal, financial seal, and the signature of any authorized officer shall be binding on the Company.

3. Registered Office Adoption. The Board adopts [●] as the registered office and statutory domicile of the Company for the service of process and all administrative and judicial communications, effective as of the date of this Resolution. A copy of this Resolution shall be maintained at the registered office.

4. Statutory Officer Appointments. [Full name] is appointed Legal Representative; [Full name] is appointed General Manager; [Full name] is appointed Supervisor; each shall serve until any subsequent shareholder resolution. The Legal Representative is authorized to execute all registration filings with the State Administration for Market Regulation, tax authorities, and other agencies.

5. General Authority. The Legal Representative, General Manager, and/or any person appointed by them are authorized to obtain the business license, company seal, patent agency license, and any required permits, to sign all declarations, leases, contracts, and applications, and to take every action necessary to carry out the foregoing resolutions.

6. Ratification. All acts performed by the sole shareholder, incorporator, and officers prior to the date of this Resolution in connection with formation of the Company are hereby ratified and confirmed.

This Resolution is effective immediately, is unconditional, and may be relied upon by third parties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-formation negative-list verification and company name reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) - National Enterprise Name Registration Online System
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the National Integrated Online Government Service Platform and the SAMR Enterprise Name Registration module. Verify that the proposed business scope, namely patent prosecution and international trademark agency services under ISIC 7490, is not on the Foreign Investment Negative List; choose a company name in the format City plus Trade Name plus Industry plus Limited Company; reserve the Chinese and English names. Complete the pre-registration questionnaire identifying jurisdiction, shareholder, and proposed scope. Submit for preliminary screening; upon approval, retain the name reservation notice for use in the formal application. If the use of China or National is desired, obtain SAMR special approval; otherwise select a municipal-level registration.
required_dossiers: Proposed Chinese company name and English name
Detailed business scope statement for ISIC 7490
Copy of the ultimate foreign shareholder's passport or certificate of incorporation
Bank account and contact data of the foreign investor
Draft Articles of Association
Preliminary registered address or renting intent letter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is refused for similarity or prohibited characters, file a fresh pre-registration with a revised name; if refusal is based on misclassification, submit a clarification; any discretionary decision can be challenged by applying for administrative reconsideration with SAMR within 60 days, or by bringing an administrative lawsuit under the Administrative Procedure Law within six months.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization, apostille or consular legalization, and certified Chinese translation of foreign investor documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public in the investor's jurisdiction; competent Apostille Authority or Chinese Embassy/Consulate
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and authenticate the foreign investor's corporate documents. If the investor is a registered entity, obtain a certified copy of its certificate of incorporation, memorandum or equivalent, and board resolution authorizing establishment of the WFOE. Have these documents notarized by a local notary; if the investor's country is a Party to the Hague Apostille Convention, affix an Apostille through the competent authority; otherwise legalize through the Chinese Embassy or Consulate. Engage a qualified translator to translate all documents into Chinese; the translation should either be included in the notarial deed or supplied as a certified translation for SAMR. Ensure passports or identity documents of all directors, supervisors, and legal representatives are notarized. Submit the full dossier to the designated authorities within the validity period; retain all receipts.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of foreign investor's Certificate of Incorporation and Memorandum or Articles
Board resolution of foreign investor authorizing WFOE establishment and signing of Articles
Power of attorney appointing the Chinese formation agent or legal representative
Passport or identity documents of investor, directors, supervisor, and legal representative
Apostille or Chinese consular legalization certificates for all foreign public documents
Certified Chinese translation of all foreign documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarized or apostilled documents are rejected due to authentication defects, cure the defect by re-executing before the original notary, obtaining a fresh Apostille or consular legalization, and delivering a supplemental certified Chinese translation; request correction to the SAMR file with a cover letter; the timeline restarts but previously filed portions remain valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Formal submission of establishment registration and issuance of business license
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local Municipal Market Supervision and Administration Bureau (SAMR registration window or online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the formal Market Entity Registration Application Form and lodge all required schedules through the local Market Supervision and Administration Bureau's online portal or physical counter. Input the Articles of Association in the prescribed format, specify registered capital, shareholder contribution schedule, governance structure, business scope, and legal representative. Upload the authenticated foreign investor documents, name reservation notice, address proof such as lease or ownership certificate, and identity documents. All natural persons involved must verify identity via electronic authentication or appear in person. Pay no official filing fee. Upon approval, the SAMR will issue a business license containing the Unified Social Credit Code. Then promptly complete the company seal engraving through a licensed seal carver, file the seal specimen with public security, and produce the official seal.
required_dossiers: Completed Market Entity Registration Application Form
Signed Articles of Association
Name reservation notice
Registered address proof (lease agreement and property ownership certificate or landlord consent)
Authenticated foreign investor documents and Chinese translations
Identity verification documents of legal representative, directors, supervisors, and general manager
Original power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration application is suspended or queried, the registration official will issue a correction notice with a remedy period; the applicant must respond within that period, attaching a revised Articles of Association or supplementary authentic evidence. If the SAMR denies registration, request administrative reconsideration or file suit; if the denial arises from negative-list non-compliance, revise the business scope and re-apply.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration bank account, tax registration, social insurance, seal filing, and foreign exchange registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank; State Taxation Administration; local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After receiving the business license, go to a licensed bank to open a RMB basic deposit account and, if needed, foreign currency account; provide the business license, unified social credit code, seal specimen, legal representative ID, and Articles of Association. Then complete tax registration with the State Taxation Administration and apply for electronic tax login within 30 days or earlier; if taxpayer status requires it, select VAT general taxpayer. File the social insurance registration and make the required employee insurances with the local Human Resources and Social Security Bureau. Where foreign exchange receipts are expected, complete registration as an FDI enterprise in the SAFE system. Obtain any statistical or industry reporting registration required by the local statistics bureau.
required_dossiers: Original business license with Unified Social Credit Code
Company seal, financial seal, legal representative seal, and seal recordation certificate
Bank account opening application and financial institution KYC forms
Tax registration forms
Social insurance registration forms
SAFE FDI registration forms if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If bank account or tax registration is delayed by inconsistent seals or legal representative ID, correct the seal and re-file, or use the unified social credit code to obtain provisional tax registration; if the system block persists, request a manual intervention from the tax service hall and, if necessary, file a written complaint with SAMR; administrative review is available for denial or refusal to process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Sectoral licensing for domestic patent agency practice before CNIPA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: State Intellectual Property Office of the People's Republic of China (CNIPA) - Patent Agency Administration Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: For domestic patent agency practice, apply to CNIPA for a Patent Agency Registration Certificate. Confirm the WFOE has at least two full-time licensed Chinese patent agents and otherwise complies with the Patent Agency Regulations; compile employment contracts, practice licenses, identity documents, premises lease, and Articles. Submit the online application or paper dossier to CNIPA's Patent Agency Management; CNIPA will inspect the agents' qualifications, the premises, and the Articles. After approval, collect the certificate and register the agency in CNIPA's public database. If the company will only prosecute patents before foreign offices and provide international trademark registration, the CNIPA patent agency license may be not applicable and the company may proceed as an IP consulting and prosecution agency; however, this step is listed because the target commercial model requires statutory licensure.
required_dossiers: CNIPA Patent Agency Registration Application Form
Business license of WFOE
Lease agreement for office premises
Employment contracts for at least two full-time licensed Chinese patent agents
Patent agent practice certificates issued by CNIPA
Identity documents and resumes of patent agents
Articles of Association and governance resolution appointing the responsible officer
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CNIPA rejects or suspends the patent agency license application, remedy by adding qualified full-time patent agents, correcting employment or premises documentation, and resubmitting within the statutory correction window; if denial is on legal disqualification, remove the disqualified director or officer; afterwards maintain a re-examination request or administrative reconsideration within 60 days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: State Intellectual Property Office of the People's Republic of China (CNIPA) as the sectoral licensing authority; no industrial manufacturing authority is implicated by ISIC 7490.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: CNIPA Patent Agency Registration Certificate (special administrative license for domestic patent prosecution); for pure international non-CNIPA prosecution and trademark registration, no physical industrial operating license is required.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable (No Environmental Permitting Agency for Office-Based Professional Services)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category 4 professional service; no construction, industrial installation or pollution-discharge facility is established; therefore no EIA registration or full EIA report is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable. The entity will generate no process wastewater, VOCs, hazardous waste, or regulated stack emissions; only municipal domestic waste and office wastewater will occur, collected by licensed municipal services. If future industrialization occurs, a fresh EIA screening would be mandatory.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office occupancy clearance: the landlord must provide a valid fire-safety inspection or acceptance certificate for the building; the WFOE, as lessee, must maintain fire extinguishers, emergency lighting, an evacuation plan, and fire-safety self-inspection records in accordance with the PRC Fire Control Law. General workplace safety registration under the Work Safety Law and occupational disease prevention obligations apply to all office employees. No civil defense shelter or special structural clearance is required for ISIC 7490.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) of the People's Republic of China; online electronic portal: Electronic Tax Bureau (e-Tax Bureau) operated under the unified STA national e-tax platform and provincial tax service websites.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the WFOE with the local State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR). The business license will bear the Unified Social Credit Code (USCC), which is simultaneously the legal entity's Tax Identification Number (TIN) and VAT registration number in the PRC tax system. Step 2: Within 30 days after license issuance, complete tax record-filing in the STA e-Tax Bureau, confirming taxpayer status for Enterprise Income Tax, VAT, urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, stamp duty, and payroll/individual income tax withholding. Step 3: Determine VAT status: if projected annual taxable sales exceed RMB 5,000,000, general VAT taxpayer registration is mandatory; below that threshold, the WFOE may elect general taxpayer status or use the small-scale taxpayer simplified method. Step 4: Register bank account details in the e-Tax system, complete accounting system filing, and apply for electronic invoice issuance capacity and VAT invoice quotas. Step 5: For a foreign non-resident enterprise without an establishment in China, the PRC payer performs withholding tax registration and the non-resident obtains a separate TIN through the e-Tax Bureau; however, in this payload the WFOE is a Chinese resident entity, so the USCC constitutes its permanent statutory TIN.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity classification. PRC law does not provide check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election mechanisms. A WFOE is automatically a resident enterprise taxed at entity level under the Enterprise Income Tax Law. For VAT only, a taxpayer below the RMB 5,000,000 annual taxable sales threshold may elect small-scale simplified taxation; this is not a corporate classification election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - PRC Value-Added Tax (multi-rate system: 13% standard rate for goods, 9% for specified goods and utilities, 6% for services, 0% for exports and qualifying cross-border services; small-scale taxpayer simplified levy available).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold for basic tax registration because a WFOE is automatically registered as a legal entity. The statutory VAT status threshold is RMB 5,000,000 in annual taxable sales for mandatory general VAT taxpayer registration; below this amount, small-scale taxpayer treatment applies, with an optional small-scale VAT exemption for monthly sales not exceeding RMB 100,000 or quarterly sales not exceeding RMB 300,000.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: China operates the STA VAT invoice management system under the Golden Tax framework. VAT invoices must be issued through the approved e-invoicing system or the e-Tax Bureau in digital form. Full Digital Electronic Invoices are integrated with the STA real-time clearance and validation engine; each invoice carries a unique tax control number and anti-counterfeit QR code, and invoice data is transmitted to the national VAT electronic invoice platform as a condition of validity. ERP and accounting systems may use authorized machine-to-machine interfaces/API-style integration for invoice issuance and data reporting. Third-party manual stamping cannot replace the digital tax-control marking; invoices must be verified through the National VAT Invoice Verification Platform.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: For goods: 0% VAT applies when goods are actually exported from China, the export is evidenced by a Customs export declaration, the exporter is a registered VAT taxpayer, transport documentation confirms movement out of China, and foreign-currency export proceeds are repatriated through bank channels. For cross-border services: zero-rating or VAT exemption is available only for services expressly listed in the STA cross-border taxable service catalogue, such as international transport, research and development, software design, and certain qualifying digital/information services, provided the service recipient is a non-resident enterprise, the services are consumed outside China, and documentary proof is retained. Patent prosecution and international trademark registration agency services are not automatically zero-rated; they are generally treated as taxable services at 6% unless a separate qualifying cross-border service category is met. If the service does not qualify, output VAT must be charged and paid.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Goods Declaration Form filed through the Customs Single Window system
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill or equivalent transport document evidencing export movement from China
Commercial invoice / export contract or service agreement
VAT special invoice or ordinary VAT invoice issued for the export or cross-border supply
Bank foreign-exchange collection certificate, settlement/verification document, or foreign-currency bank statement evidencing receipt from an overseas party within the repatriation deadline
For cross-border services: engagement letter, service performance documentation, and a statement confirming the non-resident recipient and offshore consumption
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The STA and the General Administration of Customs may jointly audit export VAT refund and zero-rating claims. Unverified or fraudulent export zero-rating results in immediate clawback of the input VAT refunded and output VAT underdeclared, plus a daily late-payment surcharge of 0.05% and an administrative penalty of 50% to 500% of the evaded tax under the Law on the Administration of Tax Collection. Fraudulent export rebate claims also trigger criminal liability under Article 204 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, including fines, confiscation, and imprisonment. The look-back period for tax fraud is unlimited; for non-fraudulent underpayments, the general clawback window is 3 to 5 years.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) of the People's Republic of China, operating under the People's Bank of China (PBOC)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: China maintains a managed floating exchange-rate regime with RMB freely convertible on current account and strictly controlled, approval-based convertibility on capital account. For a WFOE, ordinary operational payments such as IP fees, patent office charges, salaries and taxes can be settled with the bank under the current-account truthfulness review principle, provided invoices, contracts and customs or tax documents are presented. Capital account flows, including inbound equity contributions, cross-border loans, dividend remittance and liquidation proceeds, require pre-registration or approval by SAFE and are settled through dedicated bank accounts. The WFOE must first complete foreign investment registration with the local commerce bureau and Foreign Exchange Registration for Direct Investment at a designated bank. The bank then grants FDI capital account status and permits conversion only into an RMB settlement-pending account for permitted operating expenditures. Profit remittance to the overseas parent is lawful after annual statutory audit and tax clearance, but requires evidence of paid-in registered capital and proof that all statutory registration obligations are current. Withdrawal of investment or reduction of registered capital requires an additional SAFE liquidation registration and will be subject to bank verification of surplus, tax payments and creditor claims. Trade-related export receipts are not subject to a literal surrender ratio, but all such proceeds must be repatriated and banked domestically. Offshore fintech channels cannot legalise RMB conversion or replace SAFE-registered banking procedures.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the SAFE trade-in-goods monitoring regime, merchandise export receipts must be repatriated to and credited within a domestic current-account foreign exchange bank account of the exporter. Banks perform total-amount screening against customs export data and require matching customs declarations within the monitoring window, with 90 days generally applicable to advanced receipts, deferred payments and prepayment adjustments. No statutory fixed conversion ratio is imposed on export receipts; the enterprise may retain 100% of export foreign currency in its current-account foreign exchange bank account or instruct the bank to convert any amount into RMB at the prevailing market rate. If export proceeds remain unrepatriated more than 180 days after export customs clearance, the exporter must submit a written delayed collection application to the local SAFE branch together with the original trade contract, customs declaration, transport documents and the bank confirmation explaining the commercial cause.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of China Limited - Shanghai Licensed Branch
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Exchange Capital Account (FDI capital escrow) and RMB Settlement Pending Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Limited - Direct Investment Services Desk
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Capital Contribution Account and Basic Operational RMB/Foreign Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: China Merchants Bank Co., Ltd. - Head Office Corporate Banking Division
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: FDI Capital Account, Cross-Border Service Trade Settlement Account and Operating Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low and legally blocked as a primary account provider. Offshore digital EMI platforms such as Wise, Revolut and Airwallex are neither licensed nor authorised by the PBOC/SAFE to hold or settle RMB deposits for onshore Chinese entities, and no PRC anti-money laundering regime permits a WFOE to use them as its formal operational account. An offshore EMI can at best serve as an ancillary information reference or facilitate parent-side remittance initiation, but all statutory capital injections, export receipts, tax payments, patent-office disbursements and dividend remittances must move through a SAFE-designated domestic licensed bank. Using an EMI as an offshore treasury buffer without a recognised foreign exchange registration would create an unreported offshore liability and expose the WFOE to account freezing, PBOC fines and adverse KYC findings in any subsequent audit.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For the initial corporate account opening of a Chinese WFOE, at least one statutory director or legal representative must normally appear physically in a designated bank branch with an original passport or national ID, the business license, company seal, articles of association and the completed beneficial-ownership declaration. Remote consular proxy opening is not recognised for the first-time establishment of an onshore corporate account. If the legal representative is a non-resident, the bank will require an in-person AML interview to verify actual beneficial ownership and source of funds. A notarised power of attorney may later allow the operational director or company secretary to carry out additional counters, update signatories or initiate transactions, but the substantive initial onboarding interview must be completed by the statutory representative in the presence of a senior relationship manager and a compliance officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore parent structure with no clearly identifiable ultimate beneficial owner, particularly ownership layers involving BVI, Cayman or other low-disclosure jurisdictions, triggering PBOC beneficial-ownership transparency red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a notarised group ownership chart tracing control through the ultimate natural person, valid passports and national identity certificates for all signatories and beneficial owners, a PBOC-compliant beneficial-ownership declaration on the WFOE, bank reference letters for each intermediate holding entity, and, where the ultimate owner is a listed company, a stock-exchange listing document and current shareholder register extract from the relevant securities depository.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capability gap or commercial-substance confusion: the declared WFOE scope is IP patent prosecution and trademark registration, but the proposed capital profile and massive initial escrow deposits do not match the projected revenue, staffing or fee schedule of an agency.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply the Foreign Investment Filing Certificate and SAFE FDI registration confirmation, board resolutions authorising each capital call, a detailed business plan showing expected PCT and trademark workloads, hiring and office-substance plans for registered patent attorneys, a signed office lease agreement, and a pipeline of candidate patent/trademark matters supported by instruction letters from foreign clients.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border fee flows to jurisdictions or counterparties that may be subject to PRC sanctions, US OFAC sanctions, EU restrictive measures or export-control embargoes, with particular concern about payments to patent offices or law firms in risk-rated jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a sanctions and adverse-media screening report from a recognised screening provider covering all counterparties, including the international patent offices, associate law firms and inventors-paying entities; provide an internal export-control and sanctions policy manual; include the PRC patent agency licence or equivalent professional qualification certificate; and attach underlying IP case dockets, instruction contracts and invoice packages for every remittance referencing the exact SAFE service-transaction purpose code.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unverifiable personal wealth or PEP-like profile of the foreign investor where accounts, salary history or dividend records do not explain the scale of remitted capital, triggering enhanced due diligence and source-of-wealth rejection risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver audited personal or corporate financial statements for the most recent two years, twelve months of source bank statements showing the specific funding path of the remitted amounts, notarised proof of legitimate income such as employment contracts, tax returns, bonus letters or dividend vouchers, and a formal source-of-wealth declaration signed in the presence of the bank's compliance committee.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity funds must be remitted from the registered foreign investor's own overseas bank account to the WFOE's SAFE-authorised Foreign Exchange Capital Account at a domestic licensed bank using SWIFT MT103. The remittance instruction must name the WFOE, identify the SAFE FDI registration reference, and use the SAFE Balance-of-Payments transaction purpose code corresponding to inbound direct investment equity, often referred to as the FDI capital injection code under the SAFE monitoring system. Upon receipt, the bank verifies the funds against the SAFE registration record and credits the capital account; conversion to RMB is permitted only into a settlement-pending-payment account and only for the WFOE's lawful operating expenditure, infrastructure, payroll, procurement or tax liabilities. After the funds are credited, a PRC certified public accountant must issue a statutory capital contribution verification report confirming paid-in capital against the registered capital schedule, and the WFOE must then file the paid-in capital status with the Administration for Market Regulation and the national enterprise credit information system before any operating disbursement is permitted. Funds cannot be lent to shareholders, disbursed to affiliates, invested in securities, or applied to any purpose outside the registered business scope without further SAFE approval.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Patent prosecution, trademark registration and IP consulting fees due to foreign patent offices, overseas legal counsel and official registries are current-account service imports and can be cleared via SWIFT MT103 from the WFOE's operating RMB or foreign currency account after the bank completes a current-account truthfulness review. The WFOE must present the underlying service contract, the foreign invoice, the official patent or trademark submission receipt, and the correct service-trade foreign-exchange purpose code such as the code for royalties or licence fees for non-produced intellectual property. Commercial letters of credit are rarely used for agency fees but may be structured where a counterparty requires documentary security; documentary collections are permissible only when accompanied by clean financial or administrative documents such as the official filing invoice and proof of arrival of the patent/trademark response paper. For any remittance to an offshore affiliate or when cumulative annual service payments exceed the bank's monitoring threshold, the WFOE must also provide the completed service-trade and foreign-exchange income declaration and the corporate income-tax withholding or tax registration certificate to allow the bank to proceed with the outward payment.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable RMB/US dollar forward contracts executed with a SAFE-designated domestic bank, only when backed by genuine current-account trade or service income exposure and approved under the bank's real-demand derivative onboarding.
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) available to the offshore parent or offshore treasury vehicle for investor-level RMB hedging, provided the WFOE itself does not enter speculative offshore NDF trades.

Cross-currency swaps or RMB/foreign-currency interest-rate swaps for long-term capital or foreign-debt liability hedging, permitted only where the underlying foreign debt is SAFE-registered, the derivative is transacted with a domestic bank under the real-demand background and no speculative leverage is retained.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Enterprise Annual Report and Integrated Foreign Investment Information Report (年度报告及外商投资信息报告)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Administration for Market Regulation (SAMR) via the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System; jointly with the Ministry of Commerce (MOFCOM) for the Foreign Investment Information Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 through June 30 each calendar year, reporting on the immediately preceding fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to publish by June 30 results in inclusion on the List of Enterprises with Abnormal Operations within 20 working days; removal requires an application and possible departmental verification; persistent non-publication for 3 consecutive years triggers listing as a Seriously Illegal and Untrustworthy Enterprise, with restrictions on the legal representative and responsible persons, public credit degradation, and eventual administrative revocation or forced deregistration of the business license.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Annual Reconciliation and Settlement Filing (企业所得税汇算清缴)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: State Taxation Administration (STA) via the local competent tax bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before May 31 of the year following the tax year; no extension beyond this date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts a daily overdue surcharge of 0.05% on unpaid tax; penalty ranging from 50% to 5 times the underpaid amount; tax authorities may freeze bank accounts, seize assets, impose tax preservation measures, and block legal representative exits through immigration control; for continued non-compliance, tax registration may be cancelled and the company may be administratively struck off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Patent Agency Annual Business Filing and Practice License Maintainance (专利代理机构年度报告)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by April 30, covering the prior calendar year's patent agency business operations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or late filing triggers a written compliance order; repeated or material non-compliance may result in suspension or revocation of the patent agency practice license, effectively terminating the statutory right to conduct PCT and trademark prosecution work.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Financial Statement Audit and Filing of Audited Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Statutory audit report delivered to the board and shareholders; relied on by SAMR, MOFCOM and STA in the annual reporting process; not independently filed as a separate fee-bearing return except as attached to the annual report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Must be completed and available no later than June 30 of the year following the fiscal year end, in order to accompany the annual report and annual tax settlement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Absence of a legal audit report causes rejection of annual report and sets off the abnormal listing procedure and tax non-compliance penalties; directors who approve financial statements without audit may be personally liable for civil and administrative consequences.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under Article 63 of the PRC Company Law (2023 Revision) and the Foreign Investment Law Implementation Rules, every Wholly Foreign-Owned Enterprise (WFOE) is unconditionally subject to an annual statutory audit by a lawfully-established Chinese CPA firm, without any exemption based on balance sheet size, turnover, or headcount; nevertheless, mandatory audit is also triggered as a quantitative guideline when annual operating revenue exceeds RMB 200 million, total assets exceed RMB 400 million, or workforce exceeds 200 employees, and for any enterprise involved in related-party transactions with aggregate transaction value exceeding RMB 20 million, which triggers additional contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation and audit scrutiny.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Chinese Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises (CAS/ASBE), substantially convergent with IFRS; small-scale private enterprises may elect the simplified Accounting Standards for Small Enterprises, but a WFOE is generally required to apply full CAS for statutory reporting unless its scale and non-public status squarely fit the Ministry of Finance small-enterprise exemption.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The WFOE must submit initial beneficial owner information to SAMR within 30 days of incorporation, and thereafter any change in shareholding, control, or beneficial ownership must be reported within 30 days of the change. In addition, during each annual enterprise report window (January 1 to June 30), the company must reconfirm that the recorded beneficial owner information remains accurate; a false or omitted annual confirmation exposes the company to administrative penalties up to RMB 50,000, credit record blacklisting, and sanctions against directors and the legal representative.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$1,200 – US$4,800 per year for a registered address in a major commercial city plus external bookkeeping/company secretarial liaison services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$2,500 – US$8,500 per year for a WFOE with patent agency operations, depending on transaction volume, intercompany activities, and number of registered entities

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Qualified small and low-profit enterprises enjoy an effective CIT rate of 5% on taxable income not exceeding RMB 3 million with the statutory employee and asset ceilings; encouraged industries in designated regions such as free trade zones and the Western Region may access a 15% preferential rate; eligible R&D expenses may claim a 100% additional deduction; a temporary CIT exemption may apply on reinvestment of China-source profits by non-resident enterprises in encouraged industries.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form A100000 (A-Type Annual Enterprise Income Tax Return for Resident Enterprises) filed electronically through the State Taxation Administration e-Tax online filing portal, together with supplementary schedules for related-party transactions, tax preferences, and foreign tax credits.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final settlement return, supplemented by quarterly provisional prepayment returns.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual final settlement return is due within five months after the fiscal year end; each quarterly provisional prepayment return is due within fifteen days after the end of the quarter.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Sales revenue from principal operations, including patent prosecution, PCT application, and international trademark registration agency service fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Accrue revenue under the accrual method on a gross basis. Include all cross-border billings denominated in foreign currency translated into RMB at the prescribed monthly or average spot rate. Do not net out commissions payable to foreign agents unless the WFOE is the documented principal and all agency agreements, invoices, and economic substance records are retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of sales, comprising direct labor, direct professional service fees, and allocable patent office filing costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-border service fees charged by the foreign parent or affiliated entities must be supported by actual service delivery, contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, and comparability analysis. Any fee that lacks commercial substance or exceeds an arm's length amount will be disallowed and reclassified as an offshore profit distribution subject to withholding tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxes and surcharges excluding corporate income tax and VAT recoverable under input-output credit rules.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Chinese invoiced VAT, urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharges, and stamp duties directly attributable to the patent prosecution business are deductible. Withholding taxes borne or paid by the WFOE on behalf of a non-resident beneficiary are generally non-deductible unless the contract expressly shifts the burden and the payment is properly characterised as grossed-up royalties or service fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Selling expenses, including business development, marketing collateral, and overseas client acquisition costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses paid to non-resident sales agents or lead-generators require a valid contract, proof of actual service, and verification that the service is performed outside China or, if performed inside China, would give rise to a permanent establishment of the foreign provider. Deductions will be denied without proper withholding on any China-source service income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Administrative expenses, including management, legal, IT, and back-office costs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Management fees paid between related enterprises are expressly non-deductible under Chinese tax law. If the WFOE pays a foreign parent for shared services, the charge must be a properly documented cost contribution or arm's length service fee, must be within the relevant TP threshold, and must not represent a duplication of costs borne by the WFOE or its foreign related parties.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Financial expenses, including intercompany interest on shareholder loans and bank fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to non-resident related lenders is deductible only to the extent it satisfies the arm's length interest rate and the thin capitalization debt-equity ratio rules. The WFOE must withhold 10% on gross interest paid, or the treaty rate if beneficial ownership and a valid TRC are substantiated, and must report the loan transaction in the related-party schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Investment income, including interest received, dividend income from investments, and asset disposal gains.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends received from domestic Chinese investees are generally exempt from corporate income tax; dividends from non-resident investees may be taxable with a foreign tax credit claim. A WFOE must distinguish portfolio investment returns from payments to its own non-resident shareholders, as shareholder distributions are after-tax profits and are not deductible at the WFOE level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-operating income and expenditures, penalties, donations, and asset write-offs.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any waiver of intercompany receivables, foreign exchange gains, or capital gains realized from a disposal of the WFOE to a non-resident parent must be fully reported. Forgiveness of debt by a non-resident related party is generally treated as taxable non-operating income unless a formal capital increase is approved.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total accounting profit computed from the statutory profit-and-loss statement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile accounting profit to tax base; transfer pricing adjustments, thin capitalization interest disallowances, and non-deductible foreign withholding taxes must be added back. Ensure the annual related-party reporting schedule discloses all cross-border transactions with the foreign parent and affiliates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after all legal adjustments, exempt income, tax losses, and special tax adjustment items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax losses may be carried forward five years, but losses for high-tech enterprises and small technology enterprises may be carried forward ten years under qualified regimes. The WFOE may not apply any foreign parent company loss offset and must include all China-source and foreign-source income unless an exemption or treaty provision explicitly applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax payable at the statutory headline rate, after tax preferences, reductions, exemptions, and foreign tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Calculate at 25%; apply the 15% preferential rate only if the WFOE holds the relevant encouraged-industry certificate; apply the small and low-profit effective 5% rate only if all statutory employee, asset, and taxable income thresholds are met. Claim foreign tax credits on income from foreign jurisdictions only with credible evidence of foreign tax paid on the same income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credit for quarterly provisional prepayments and the final balance of tax payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Reconcile the annual payable with all quarterly payments; a balance due must be paid before or on May 31. A refund claim of overpaid tax attributable to non-resident withheld tax or treaty reduction must be filed before the expiry of the three-year statutory refund limitation period.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalties range from RMB 2,000 to RMB 10,000; late payment of tax attracts a daily surcharge of 0.05% (approximately 18.25% annualized). Under-reporting or underpayment caused by negligence or deliberate fraud triggers administrative penalties of 50% to 500% of the additional tax amount, and criminal prosecution under Article 201 of the PRC Criminal Law can arise if the evaded tax reaches the statutory criminal threshold, exposing responsible directors to fines and imprisonment.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Withholding Enterprise Income Tax Return for Non-Resident Enterprises (withholding at source form) filed through the same State Taxation Administration e-Tax portal by the WFOE as the statutory withholding agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Event-driven, filed in respect of each outbound remittance of China-source dividends, interest, royalties, rents, capital gains, or other income to a non-resident enterprise that has no permanent establishment in China.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The withholding return and payment must be filed within seven days from the date the withholding obligation arises, normally the earlier of the date of payment to the non-resident, the date the amount becomes due, or the date the liability is determined contractually.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding agent identification data, social credit code, and filing period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The WFOE must use its Chinese unified social credit code and ensure the filing period corresponds to the date the outbound payment is actually made or becomes due. Late filing of a nil withholding return should be avoided because the obligation is event-triggered.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident payee identification, tax residency jurisdiction, and tax identification number in the home jurisdiction.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Identify the true beneficial owner of the income, not merely the contracting party. If an intermediary or agent receives the payment, the WFOE must obtain a beneficial ownership declaration and documentary chain. An intermediary without substance will not qualify for treaty relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income category code, indicating whether the remittance is dividend, interest, royalty, service fee, rent, or capital gain.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Accurate source classification is critical. Royalties for the right to use patents, trademarks, or know-how in China are China-source income taxable at 10% or the applicable treaty rate; payments that are disguised as service fees or reimbursement of expenses may be recharacterized by the tax authority as royalties or dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross amount of China-source income subject to withholding, expressed in RMB after currency translation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Withhold on the gross contractual amount before any foreign or domestic taxes, fees, or discount charges. If the WFOE agrees to bear the foreign tax, the taxable base must be grossed up to the amount that would yield the agreed net payment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable tax rate, either the statutory 10% rate or a reduced bilateral DTA rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The statutory withholding rate is 10%. Reduced treaty rates may be applied only when the non-resident is the beneficial owner and supplies a valid Tax Residency Certificate and any additional treaty benefit declarations required by the State Taxation Administration. The WFOE must keep the supporting evidence on file and make it available on inspection.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax amount withheld and paid over to the State Treasury.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The amount must be paid electronically within seven days. If the WFOE fails to withhold but the non-resident later pays the tax, the WFOE may still face the statutory penalty for failure to withhold, plus late surcharges if the payment was made late.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Treaty relief particulars, including DTA article, treaty country, TRC reference, and beneficial ownership statement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the Tax Residency Certificate issued by the foreign competent authority, a statement that the non-resident is the beneficial owner of the dividend, interest, or royalty, and evidence that the foreign entity has economic substance in its jurisdiction. Any false statement or fabricated TRC will void the treaty claim and expose the WFOE and its directors to administrative and criminal liability.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to withhold or to pay over withheld tax triggers a daily late surcharge of 0.05% and an administrative fine of 50% to 300% of the amount under-withheld under Article 69 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law. Misdeclaration of a China-source payment as non-taxable offshore income can be recast by the tax authority as a taxable Chinese-source payment, with additional corporate income tax, interest, penalties of up to 500%, and potential criminal liability under Article 201 of the PRC Criminal Law.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% gross withholding tax on dividends paid by the WFOE to a non-resident corporate shareholder that has no permanent establishment in China, reduced under an applicable bilateral DTA if the shareholder is the beneficial owner.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident shareholder must submit a treaty benefit application through the withholding agent, provide the Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the competent tax authority of the treaty country, complete a beneficial ownership declaration supported by economic substance documentation, and identify the specific DTA article conferring the reduced rate. The WFOE must withhold at the reduced treaty rate only after the e-Tax system or the local tax authority accepts the claim; otherwise, the statutory 10% must be withheld. All TRC and beneficial ownership records must be retained for at least ten years and produced to the State Taxation Administration upon inspection. If the TRC expires, is incomplete, or the foreign recipient lacks substance, the DTA relief is denied and the full 10% plus late surcharges become due.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: The statutory withholding rate on China-source royalties and interest paid to non-resident enterprises is 10% on the gross amount. Under the China-Hong Kong DTA, the treaty rate is 5% for royalties and 7% for interest, provided the beneficial ownership test is met; under other DTAs the rate may be reduced to 0%, 5%, 7%, or 10% depending on the income type, ownership threshold, and treaty terms. Royalties arising from the use of patents, know-how, trademarks, or copyrights in China are Chinese-source income, and intercompany interest is China-source income when paid by a Chinese resident borrower.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: RMB 100,000,000 for tangible asset transfers, RMB 10,000,000 for intangible property transfers and service transactions, and RMB 1,000,000,000 aggregate related-party transactions for Master File preparation, as revised by SAT Announcement [2016] No. 42; a WFOE must also file the Annual Related Party Transaction Report when any related-party transactions exist, irrespective of the documentation thresholds.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: China does not administer a separate UAE-style Economic Substance Regulations registration regime, but the statutory General Anti-Avoidance Rules, the special tax adjustment regime, and the treaty beneficial ownership doctrine require the WFOE and any non-resident intermediate holding company to perform substantive Core Income-Generating Activities (CIGA) in the claimed jurisdiction. A patent prosecution WFOE must maintain qualified employees, physical premises, decision-making authority, business risk assumption, and contemporaneous records proving that services and intangible property transfers were actually performed and compensated at arm's length. Entities lacking such substance will be denied treaty benefits and may be recharacterized under Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing manipulation and tax evasion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE deducts an inflated patent search and preparation service fee from its foreign parent or affiliated IP holding company, materially overstating expenses and shifting China-source profit offshore while no substantive service is rendered and no contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation is prepared.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A special tax adjustment under Article 41 and Article 48 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law imposes upward pricing adjustments, imputed interest at market rates, and an administrative penalty of 50% to 500% of the underpaid tax under Article 63 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law. Repeated or intentional conduct reaching the criminal threshold triggers prosecution under Article 201 of the PRC Criminal Law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil may be pierced if directors signed or knowingly approved the false invoices and pricing arrangements; directors are jointly and severally liable for civil restitution of the unpaid tax. The legal representative is blacklisted, placed under an exit ban, and prohibited from leaving China until the tax liabilities are settled; fraudulent conduct after the criminal threshold is met carries imprisonment of up to seven years plus fines and confiscation of personal assets.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company and DTA treaty shopping
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The non-resident parent establishes or uses a zero-substance intermediate holding company in a treaty jurisdiction, with no employees, premises, economic risk, or business decision-making, solely to hold the WFOE and receive dividend distributions, and then claims the reduced 5% treaty withholding rate by presenting a Tax Residency Certificate and a paper-only beneficial ownership statement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax authority will deny treaty benefits on the basis of the OECD Principal Purpose Test and the Chinese beneficial ownership doctrine, recharacterize the intermediary under the General Anti-Avoidance Rule of Article 47 of the Enterprise Income Tax Law, and assess the 10% statutory withholding tax on the full dividend stream, plus daily late surcharges and fines of 50% to 500% if the arrangement is characterized as fraudulent tax avoidance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who structured, approved, or signed the shareholder resolutions and remittance instructions for the sham holding structure are jointly and severally liable for the additional withholding tax and civil damages. The legal representative is placed on the tax blacklist with an international exit ban; deliberate falsification of treaty benefit claims is criminal fraud under Articles 201 and 264 of the PRC Criminal Law, exposing directors to imprisonment of up to seven years and personal asset forfeiture.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding tax non-compliance and false non-resident tax declaration
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: The WFOE remits dividends, royalties, or interest to its foreign parent without withholding the statutory 10% tax, falsely classifies the payments as non-assessable offshore service charges or reimbursement of expenses, and fails to file the non-resident withholding tax return within the statutory seven-day period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 69 of the Tax Collection and Administration Law, the WFOE as withholding agent is fined 50% to 300% of the amount under-withheld and must pay the unpaid tax, plus a daily surcharge of 0.05%; if the false classification is found to be deliberate concealment, Article 63 penalties of 50% to 500% apply and the case can be referred for criminal prosecution under Article 201 of the PRC Criminal Law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved the remittance instructions, signed the foreign payment agreements, or directed the accounting treatment are personally liable for civil restitution where the WFOE lacks assets to satisfy the reinforced tax assessment; the legal representative is blacklisted and barred from exiting China until liabilities are discharged; knowing participation in the false withholding declaration carries criminal liability with imprisonment of up to seven years and personal fines, extending the pierce of the corporate veil to personal bank accounts and assets.
